Bazaar Ghar ka revenue kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Agent wale business mein revenue sirf commission: ₹30 crore × 10% = ₹3 crore. Apna inventory bechne par company khud seller hai, to poori ₹8 crore sale revenue hai. Ad fees bhi apni fees hai: ₹1 crore. Total = 3 + 8 + 1 = ₹12 crore, option D. Option A poore GMV ko revenue maan leta hai. Option B apni direct sales bhool jaata hai. Option C GMV aur direct sales jod deta hai, fees aur commission logic dono chhod kar.

questions.question: Fictional 'Sahyog Traders' ki shuruaat mein Assets ₹100 lakh = Liabilities ₹40 lakh + Equity ₹60 lakh. Phir: (i) bank se ₹20 lakh loan liya; (ii) ₹15 lakh ka maal credit par khareeda; (iii) ₹6 lakh cost ka maal ₹10 lakh cash mein becha; (iv) ₹3 lakh rent cash mein diya; (v) ₹5 lakh loan chukaaya. Ab total assets aur equity kitne hain?
questions.explanation: Assets: 100 + 20 (cash) + 15 (inventory) + 10 − 6 (cash aaya, inventory gayi) − 3 (rent) − 5 (repayment) = 131. Liabilities: 40 + 20 + 15 − 5 = 70. Equity: 60 + 4 (gross profit) − 3 (rent expense) = 61. Check: 70 + 61 = 131, option A. Option B sale ke ₹10 lakh poore profit maan leta hai (inventory ka ₹6 lakh nikalna bhool kar). Option C loan repayment ko expense samajh leta hai; repayment sirf cash aur liability ghataata hai. Option D repayment do baar ghataata hai.

questions.question: Fictional 'Jyoti Packaging' ka financial year 31 March ko khatam hota hai. (i) March ki electricity ka ₹60,000 bill April mein aaya aur April mein pay hua. (ii) 1 January ko 12 mahine ka insurance premium ₹1,20,000 cash mein diya. Cash-basis dashboard in dono ka FY expense ₹1,20,000 dikhata hai. Accrual basis par in dono items ka FY expense kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Matching: expense us period ka jisme service use hui. March ki electricity is FY ki hai, chahe cash April mein gaya: ₹60,000. Insurance ke 12 mein se sirf 3 mahine (Jan–Mar) is FY mein: ₹1,20,000 × 3 ÷ 12 = ₹30,000; baaki ₹90,000 agle saal ka prepaid asset. Total = ₹90,000, option A. Option C cash-basis number hai. Option B dono ko poora expense maan leta hai. Option D sirf insurance ka hissa leta hai, electricity accrual bhool kar.

weeks.title: From Transactions to Statements: Recording, Inventory, Depreciation and Cash Flow
weeks.summary: Is week aap accounts ke types aur debit-credit rules, journal se trial balance tak ka flow, inventory valuation (FIFO, weighted average), depreciation, aur ek transaction ka balance sheet, income statement aur cash flow statement teeno par asar trace karna seekhoge.
concepts: **Types of accounts**: modern classification paanch hai: asset, liability, equity, revenue (income), expense. **Debit** assets aur expenses (aur dividends/drawings) ko badhata hai; **credit** liabilities, equity aur revenue ko badhata hai. Indian textbooks ka traditional system (personal, real, nominal accounts aur unke golden rules) bhi wahi entries deta hai, sirf yaad rakhne ka tareeka alag hai.

**Recording cycle**: transaction → journal entry (date, debit account, credit account, amount) → ledger (har account ka running balance) → trial balance (saare debit balances = saare credit balances) → adjustments (accruals, depreciation) → financial statements. ERP ye sab automatically karta hai; analyst ko general ledger table milta hai jisme account code, cost centre, debit aur credit columns hote hain.

**Inventory valuation**: COGS = opening inventory + purchases − closing inventory. **FIFO** maanta hai pehle aaya maal pehle bika; **weighted average** sab units ki average cost lagata hai. Badhti prices mein FIFO ka COGS kam, profit aur closing inventory zyada hota hai. Ind AS 2 mein LIFO allowed nahi hai. Inventory 'lower of cost and net realisable value' par dikhaayi jaati hai.

**Depreciation**: long-life asset ka cost uski useful life par expense banana. Straight-line (SLM) = (cost − residual value) ÷ life, har saal barabar; written-down value (WDV) = fixed rate × opening carrying amount, shuru mein zyada. Depreciation EBIT aur profit ko ghataata hai, EBITDA ko nahi, aur ye **non-cash** expense hai: cash to asset khareedte waqt hi gaya tha.

**Teen statements**: **balance sheet** (date par assets, liabilities, equity), **income statement** (period ka revenue aur expenses), **cash flow statement** (period ka cash teen hisson mein: operating, investing, financing). Link: net profit retained earnings mein jaata hai; cash flow ka closing cash balance sheet ke cash se match karta hai.

**Transaction trace karna**: har transaction ke liye poochho: (1) balance sheet ki kaunsi lines badli, (2) kya ye revenue ya expense hai (income statement), (3) kya cash hila, aur kis activity mein (cash flow). Credit sale revenue aur receivables badhata hai, cash nahi. Supplier ko payment cash aur payables dono ghataata hai, profit ko nahi.

**Indirect method CFO**: net profit se shuru karo, non-cash items (depreciation) wapas jodo, aur working capital changes adjust karo: current asset (receivables, inventory) badhe to ghatao, current liability (payables) badhe to jodo. Investing mein asset purchase/sale, financing mein loans, share issue aur dividends.

example.problem: Fictional 'Neelgiri Tea Co.' ke ek mahine ke transactions: (1) ₹4,00,000 ki tea stock credit par khareedi; (2) aadha stock (cost ₹2,00,000) ₹3,20,000 mein becha: ₹2,00,000 cash, ₹1,20,000 credit; (3) supplier ko ₹2,50,000 diye; (4) packing machine par ₹15,000 depreciation; (5) ₹60,000 salaries cash mein. Teeno statements par asar nikaalo.
steps: Income statement: revenue ₹3,20,000 − COGS ₹2,00,000 − salaries ₹60,000 − depreciation ₹15,000 = profit ₹45,000.
Cash: +₹2,00,000 (sale) − ₹2,50,000 (supplier) − ₹60,000 (salaries) = −₹1,10,000, poora operating activity mein.
Balance sheet assets: inventory +₹2,00,000 (4,00,000 aaya, 2,00,000 bika), receivables +₹1,20,000, machine −₹15,000, cash −₹1,10,000: total +₹1,95,000.
Liabilities + equity: payables +₹1,50,000 (4,00,000 − 2,50,000), retained earnings +₹45,000: total +₹1,95,000. Equation balance.
Indirect CFO check: 45,000 + 15,000 (depreciation) − 2,00,000 (inventory badhi) − 1,20,000 (receivables badhe) + 1,50,000 (payables badhe) = −₹1,10,000.
Answer: profit **₹45,000** par operating cash flow **−₹1,10,000**; farq inventory aur receivables mein phansa paisa hai.

mistakes: Profit ko cash samajhna. Credit sales aur inventory build-up profit dikhate hain par cash nahi laate; hamesha cash flow statement saath mein dekho.
Indirect method mein working capital ke sign ulte lagana. Current asset badhna = cash ruk gaya (ghatao); current liability badhna = cash abhi nahi diya (jodo).
Depreciation ko cash outflow maan lena. Cash asset khareedte waqt investing activity mein gaya tha; depreciation sirf us cost ko periods mein baant-ta hai.
revision: Debit: assets, expenses badhe; credit: liabilities, equity, revenue badhe.
COGS = opening + purchases − closing inventory.
Badhti prices: FIFO → kam COGS, zyada profit.
SLM = (cost − residual) ÷ life; WDV = rate × opening carrying amount.
CFO (indirect) = profit + depreciation − current asset increase + current liability increase.
Cash flow: operating, investing, financing.

questions.question: Fictional shop 'Gulmohar Crockery' ne supplier se ₹75,000 ka maal credit par khareeda. Sahi journal entry kya hai?
questions.explanation: Inventory (asset) badhi, isliye debit; supplier ko dena hai, yaani liability badhi, isliye credit: option C. Option B cash purchase ki entry hai; yahan cash abhi gaya hi nahi. Option A sides ulat deta hai, aur option D mein cash aaya dikhaya hai jo hua hi nahi.

questions.question: Ek fictional company is saal machines par ₹5 lakh depreciation record karti hai. Tax ko ignore karo. Is depreciation entry ka is saal ke cash par kya asar hai?
options: Investing activities mein ₹5 lakh ka outflow aayega
Cash par koi seedha asar nahi; ye non-cash expense hai
questions.explanation: Depreciation sirf machine ki cost ko saalon mein expense banata hai; is entry mein koi cash nahi hilta, option D. Cash machine khareedte waqt investing activity mein gaya tha. Option B indirect method mein depreciation 'add back' hone se aata hai, par add-back sirf non-cash expense ko hataata hai, cash paida nahi karta.

questions.question: Fictional retailer 'Prism Optics' ke paas opening inventory 200 frames @ ₹300 thi; phir 300 frames @ ₹340 khareede. Period mein 350 frames ₹500 each mein bike. Weighted average (periodic) method se gross profit kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Average cost = (200 × 300 + 300 × 340) ÷ 500 = ₹324. COGS = 350 × 324 = ₹1,13,400. Revenue = 350 × 500 = ₹1,75,000. Gross profit = ₹61,600, option B. Option A FIFO ka answer hai (COGS ₹1,11,000). Option C saari units latest price ₹340 par lagaata hai. Option D closing inventory ki value (150 × 324) hai, profit nahi.

questions.question: Ek fictional company ne saal ki shuruaat mein ₹8 lakh ki machine khareedi (life 5 saal, residual zero). Pehle saal ke liye do options compare karo: SLM, ya 30% WDV. Pehle saal ke EBIT aur EBITDA par kya farak padega?
options: SLM mein EBIT ₹80,000 zyada; EBITDA dono mein same
WDV mein EBIT ₹80,000 zyada; EBITDA dono mein same
SLM mein EBIT ₹80,000 zyada, aur EBITDA bhi ₹80,000 zyada
Koi farak nahi, kyunki poori life mein total depreciation barabar hai
questions.explanation: SLM depreciation = 8,00,000 ÷ 5 = ₹1,60,000; WDV = 30% × 8,00,000 = ₹2,40,000. SLM mein ₹80,000 kam expense, isliye EBIT ₹80,000 zyada, option A. EBITDA depreciation se pehle ka number hai, isliye dono methods mein same; option C yahi bhoolta hai. Option D sahi hai ki poori life ka total depreciation barabar hai, par saal-dar-saal timing alag hoti hai.

questions.question: Fictional wholesaler ne ₹60,000 cost ka maal ₹90,000 mein credit par becha. Is ek transaction ka asar kya hai?
options: Profit ₹30,000 badha, receivables ₹90,000 badhe, inventory ₹60,000 ghati, cash same raha
questions.explanation: Revenue ₹90,000 − COGS ₹60,000 = profit ₹30,000. Paisa abhi nahi mila, isliye receivables ₹90,000 badhe aur cash same; maal gaya, isliye inventory ₹60,000 ghati. Assets ka net badlaav +₹30,000 = equity ka badlaav: option B. Options A aur D credit sale ko cash maan lete hain; option C COGS bhool jaata hai.

questions.question: Fictional company 'Indus Tiles' ka opening cash ₹5 lakh hai. Saal mein: net profit ₹8 lakh; depreciation ₹2 lakh; trade receivables ₹3 lakh badhe; trade payables ₹1 lakh badhe; ₹6 lakh ki machine cash mein khareedi; ₹1 lakh loan chukaaya; ₹2 lakh dividend diya. Closing cash kitna hai?
questions.explanation: CFO = 8 + 2 − 3 + 1 = ₹8 lakh. CFI = −₹6 lakh. CFF = −1 − 2 = −₹3 lakh. Closing cash = 5 + 8 − 6 − 3 = ₹4 lakh, option C. Option A depreciation add-back bhool jaata hai. Option B receivables ke badhne ko jod deta hai (sign ulta). Option D dividend ko cash outflow nahi maanta.

questions.question: Modern classification (asset, liability, equity, revenue, expense) mein inme se kaunsa account credit karne se badhta hai?
questions.explanation: Credit liabilities, equity aur revenue ko badhata hai, isliye sales revenue, option C. Options A aur D assets hain aur option B expense; ye teeno debit se badhte hain.

questions.question: Fictional 'Pushp Foods' ne bank se ₹10 lakh ka term loan liya. Cash flow statement mein ye ₹10 lakh inflow kis activity mein dikhega?
options: Kisi activity mein nahi; ye non-cash hai
questions.explanation: Loans, share issue aur dividends financing activities hain, option D. Option A business ke roz ke cash (customers, suppliers, salaries) ke liye hai. Option B assets ki khareed ya bikri ke liye. Option C galat hai kyunki bank se asli cash aaya hai.

questions.question: Jab purchase prices lagataar badh rahi hon, to weighted average method ke comparison mein FIFO method ka COGS aur profit kaisa hoga?
options: COGS kam, closing inventory bhi kam
questions.explanation: FIFO mein pehle aaye (saste) units pehle bikte maane jaate hain, isliye COGS kam aur profit zyada, option A; closing inventory mein naye mehenge units bachte hain, to woh zyada hoti hai. Option B ulta hai. Option D sahi COGS ke saath closing inventory ki direction galat batata hai.

questions.question: Fictional 'Vaibhav Prints' ne ₹10 lakh ki printing machine khareedi: useful life 6 saal, residual value ₹1 lakh, straight-line depreciation. 2 saal baad machine ka carrying amount kitna hoga?
questions.explanation: Annual depreciation = (₹10 lakh − ₹1 lakh) ÷ 6 = ₹1.5 lakh. 2 saal baad = 10 − 3 = ₹7 lakh, option B. Option A residual value ghataana bhool jaata hai (10 ÷ 6 per saal). Option C sirf ek saal ka depreciation ghataata hai. Option D ₹2 lakh per saal maan leta hai.

questions.question: Fictional 'Deepak Lights' ke paas opening inventory 100 bulbs @ ₹50 thi; phir 200 bulbs @ ₹60 khareede. Period mein 180 bulbs bike. FIFO method se COGS aur closing inventory kya hai?
questions.explanation: FIFO: pehle purane 100 @ ₹50 = ₹5,000, phir 80 @ ₹60 = ₹4,800; COGS = ₹9,800. Bache 120 @ ₹60 = ₹7,200, option B. Check: 9,800 + 7,200 = 17,000 = total cost. Option A LIFO hai (naye pehle), jo Ind AS 2 mein allowed bhi nahi. Option C weighted average hai (₹56.67 per bulb). Option D sab units ko ₹50 par value karta hai.

questions.question: Fictional 'Ganga Mills' ne ₹10 lakh ki machine khareedi aur 20% written-down value (WDV) method se depreciation lagaati hai. Teesre saal ka depreciation aur teesre saal ke end par carrying amount kya hai?
questions.explanation: WDV = rate × opening carrying amount. Saal 1: 20% × 10 = 2, closing 8. Saal 2: 20% × 8 = 1.6, closing 6.4. Saal 3: 20% × 6.4 = 1.28, closing 5.12. Option C. Option A har saal original cost par 20% (SLM jaisa) lagata hai. Option B doosre saal ke numbers hain. Option D sahi depreciation ke saath teesre saal ka opening amount (closing nahi) deta hai.

questions.question: Fictional 'Aakar Hardware' ka saal ka net profit ₹12 lakh hai aur depreciation ₹3 lakh. Working capital: trade receivables ₹2 lakh ghate, inventory ₹4 lakh badhi, trade payables ₹1 lakh ghate. Indirect method se operating cash flow (CFO) kitna hai?
questions.explanation: CFO = 12 + 3 (depreciation wapas) + 2 (receivables ghate, cash aaya) − 4 (inventory badhi, cash phansa) − 1 (payables ghate, cash gaya) = ₹12 lakh, option A. Option B saare working capital signs ulte laga deta hai (12 + 3 − 2 + 4 + 1). Option C depreciation wapas jodna bhool jaata hai. Option D receivables ke ghatne ko bhi ghata deta hai (12 + 3 − 2 − 4 − 1).

questions.question: Fictional 'Kumud Traders' ke ek mahine mein: (1) supplier ka ₹2 lakh ka purana payable cash mein chukaaya; (2) ₹2 lakh cost ka maal ₹3 lakh mein credit par becha; (3) shop equipment par ₹0.5 lakh depreciation; (4) ₹4 lakh ki naya machine cash mein khareedi. Mahine ka profit, operating cash flow aur investing cash flow kya hai?
options: Profit ₹1 lakh; CFO −₹2 lakh; investing −₹4 lakh
Profit ₹0.5 lakh; CFO −₹2.5 lakh; investing −₹4 lakh
Profit ₹0.5 lakh; CFO ₹1 lakh; investing −₹4 lakh
Profit ₹0.5 lakh; CFO −₹2 lakh; investing −₹4 lakh
questions.explanation: Profit = 3 − 2 (COGS) − 0.5 (depreciation) = ₹0.5 lakh. Operating cash: sirf supplier payment −₹2 lakh (sale credit par thi, depreciation non-cash). Machine −₹4 lakh investing mein. Option D. Indirect check: 0.5 + 0.5 − 3 (receivables) + 2 (inventory ghati) − 2 (payables ghate) = −2. Option A depreciation bhool jaata hai. Option B depreciation ko cash outflow maan leta hai. Option C credit sale ko cash maan leta hai.

questions.question: Fictional 'Lalit Garments' (₹ lakh): opening inventory 80, purchases 300, revenue 450. Year-end stock count mein closing inventory galti se 70 likh di gayi, jabki sahi 60 hai. Reported gross profit aur sahi gross profit kitna hai?
questions.explanation: COGS = opening + purchases − closing. Reported: 80 + 300 − 70 = 310, gross profit = 450 − 310 = 140. Sahi: 80 + 300 − 60 = 320, gross profit = 130. Closing inventory ₹10 lakh zyada likhne se COGS ₹10 lakh kam aur profit ₹10 lakh zyada dikhta hai, option C. Options A aur D direction ulti kar dete hain. Option B reported sahi nikaalta hai par sahi profit mein error ulta laga deta hai.

weeks.title: Ratio Analysis: Liquidity, Solvency, Efficiency, Profitability and Valuation
weeks.summary: Is week aap financial statements se paanch families ke ratios (liquidity, solvency, efficiency, profitability, market valuation) nikaalna, unki definitions consistent rakhna, aur trend aur peers ke saath interpret karna seekhoge.
concepts: **Ratio kyun**: absolute numbers alag size ki companies ko compare nahi karne dete; ratios karte hain. Par ek ratio akela kuch nahi kehta: use **trend** (pichhle saal), **peers** (same industry) aur **business model** ke saath padho. Grocery retailer ka 0.8 current ratio normal ho sakta hai, machine maker ke liye chinta ki baat.

**Liquidity** (short-term dues chukane ki capacity): current ratio = current assets ÷ current liabilities; quick ratio = (current assets − inventories − prepaid expenses) ÷ current liabilities; cash ratio = cash and equivalents ÷ current liabilities.

**Solvency / leverage** (long-term survival): debt-equity = total borrowings ÷ equity; debt ÷ EBITDA (kitne saal ki operating earnings mein debt chuk sakta hai); interest coverage = EBIT ÷ interest expense. Zyada leverage ROE badha sakta hai, par risk bhi badhata hai.

**Efficiency / activity**: asset turnover = revenue ÷ average total assets; inventory turnover = COGS ÷ average inventory; receivables days (DSO) = receivables ÷ revenue × 365; payables days = payables ÷ COGS (ya purchases) × 365. Ye batate hain ki assets aur working capital kitni tezi se revenue aur cash mein badalte hain.

**Profitability**: gross margin, EBITDA margin, net margin (PAT ÷ revenue); ROA = PAT ÷ average total assets = net margin × asset turnover; ROE = PAT ÷ average equity; ROCE = EBIT ÷ capital employed (equity + debt). Margin aur turnover ka trade-off: discount retailer kam margin, high turnover; luxury brand ulta.

**Market valuation** (listed companies): EPS = (PAT − preference dividend) ÷ equity shares; P/E = share price ÷ EPS; book value per share = equity ÷ shares, P/B = price ÷ BVPS; dividend yield = DPS ÷ price; payout ratio = DPS ÷ EPS. **Enterprise value (EV)** = market capitalisation + debt − cash; EV/EBITDA leverage alag hone par bhi companies compare karne deta hai.

**Analyst hygiene**: har ratio ki definition data dictionary mein likho (closing ya average balance, 365 ya 360 din, total ya sirf interest-bearing debt). Numerator aur denominator same period aur same scope (standalone vs consolidated) ke hon. Quarterly flow ko annualise karke annual balance ke saath compare karo. One-off items (asset sale gain) ko alag dikhao, warna margin ka trend jhootha dikhega.

example.problem: Fictional listed company 'Ruchi Foods Ltd' (₹ crore): revenue 500, EBITDA 75, depreciation 15, interest 10, tax 25%; current assets 150 (inventory 60), current liabilities 100, borrowings 120, equity 300, cash 20; 5 crore equity shares, share price ₹120, dividend ₹3 per share. Ek ratio dashboard banao.
steps: Liquidity: current ratio = 150 ÷ 100 = 1.5; quick ratio = (150 − 60) ÷ 100 = 0.9.
Solvency: debt-equity = 120 ÷ 300 = 0.4; interest coverage = 60 ÷ 10 = 6.
Profitability: net margin = 37.5 ÷ 500 = 7.5%; ROE (closing equity) = 37.5 ÷ 300 = 12.5%.
EV = market cap (5 × 120 = 600) + debt 120 − cash 20 = 700; EV/EBITDA = 700 ÷ 75 ≈ 9.33.
Answer: **CR 1.5, QR 0.9, D/E 0.4, ICR 6, net margin 7.5%, ROE 12.5%, P/E 16, P/B 2, EV/EBITDA ≈ 9.33**. Akele ye 'achha' ya 'bura' nahi; peers aur trend ke saath padho.

mistakes: Average aur closing balances ko mix karna, ya ek company ka ratio average se aur peer ka closing se nikaalna. Ek definition chuno aur sab par lagao.
EPS ki jagah total PAT se P/E nikaal dena. P/E per-share ratio hai: share price ÷ EPS.
EV mein cash jod dena. EV = market cap + debt − cash, kyunki khareedne wale ko company ka cash mil jaata hai.
revision: Liquidity: current, quick, cash ratio.
Solvency: D/E, debt ÷ EBITDA, interest coverage (EBIT ÷ interest).
ROA = net margin × asset turnover.
P/E = price ÷ EPS; P/B = price ÷ BVPS.
Dividend yield = DPS ÷ price; payout = DPS ÷ EPS.
EV = market cap + debt − cash.

questions.question: Fictional listed company 'Avani Cements' ka PAT ₹48 crore hai aur 2 crore equity shares hain (koi preference shares nahi). Share price ₹360 hai. P/E ratio kya hai?
questions.explanation: EPS = 48 ÷ 2 = ₹24. P/E = 360 ÷ 24 = 15, option A. Option B price ko total PAT (₹48 crore) se divide karne ka trap hai; P/E per-share ratio hai. Option C EPS khud hai, aur option D ulta ratio (EPS ÷ price), jo earnings yield hai.

questions.question: Kis pair mein dono ratios solvency (long-term leverage aur debt servicing) measure karte hain?
options: Debt-equity ratio aur interest coverage ratio
questions.explanation: Debt-equity capital structure mein debt ka hissa dikhata hai aur interest coverage batata hai ki earnings interest ko kitni baar cover karti hain: dono solvency, option B. Option A liquidity (short-term) ratios hain; ye common trap hai kyunki 'paisa chukane ki capacity' dono mein hai. Option C efficiency aur option D market valuation ratios hain.

questions.question: Fictional company 'Kiran Pharma' ka EPS ₹15 hai, usne ₹6 per share dividend diya, aur share price ₹240 hai. Dividend yield aur payout ratio kya hain?
questions.explanation: Dividend yield = DPS ÷ price = 6 ÷ 240 = 2.5%. Payout = DPS ÷ EPS = 6 ÷ 15 = 40%. Option D. Option B mein 6.25% earnings yield (15 ÷ 240) hai, dividend yield nahi. Option A dono labels ulat deta hai, aur option C payout ko ulta (EPS ÷ DPS) nikaalta hai.

questions.question: Fictional distributor 'Sangam Traders' ka revenue ₹9 crore, average total assets ₹6 crore aur net profit margin 5% hai. ROA (PAT ÷ average total assets) kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Asset turnover = 9 ÷ 6 = 1.5. ROA = net margin × asset turnover = 5% × 1.5 = 7.5% (PAT = ₹0.45 crore, ÷ ₹6 crore). Option C. Option A margin ko turnover se divide karta hai, option B margin ko hi ROA maan leta hai, aur option D margin ko assets ki raqam (6) se multiply kar deta hai.

questions.question: Fictional company 'Sheetal Appliances' ki total equity ₹50 crore hai aur 2 crore equity shares hain. Share price ₹80 hai. Price-to-book (P/B) ratio kya hai?
questions.explanation: Book value per share = 50 ÷ 2 = ₹25. P/B = 80 ÷ 25 = 3.2, option D. Option A price ko total equity (₹50 crore) se divide karta hai; per-share level par lana bhool gaye. Option B ulta ratio hai, aur option C sirf BVPS hai.

questions.question: Fictional company 'Orbit Telecom Services' ke 1 crore shares ₹150 par trade ho rahe hain. Borrowings ₹40 crore, cash and equivalents ₹10 crore, aur EBITDA ₹24 crore hai. EV/EBITDA kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Market cap = 1 crore × ₹150 = ₹150 crore. EV = 150 + 40 − 10 = ₹180 crore. EV/EBITDA = 180 ÷ 24 = 7.5, option A. Option B sirf market cap use karta hai (150 ÷ 24). Option C cash ko ghataane ke bajaay jod deta hai (200 ÷ 24). Option D debt bhool jaata hai (140 ÷ 24).

questions.question: Fictional 'Pavan Motors' ke current assets ₹90 crore aur current liabilities ₹60 crore hain. Current ratio kya hai?
questions.explanation: Current ratio = current assets ÷ current liabilities = 90 ÷ 60 = 1.5, option D. Option A ratio ulta (60 ÷ 90) le leta hai. Option B difference hai (working capital ₹30 crore), ratio nahi. Option C dono ko jod kar divide karne jaisi galti hai.

questions.question: Inventory turnover (COGS ÷ average inventory) ratios ki kis category mein aata hai?
questions.explanation: Inventory turnover batata hai ki inventory kitni tezi se COGS (aur aage cash) mein badalti hai; ye efficiency / activity ratio hai, option B. Option A short-term dues chukane ki capacity (current, quick ratio) hai. Option C long-term debt aur coverage, aur option D share price wale ratios (P/E, P/B).

questions.question: Fictional 'Hira Chemicals' ka EBIT ₹45 crore aur interest expense ₹9 crore hai. Interest coverage ratio kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Interest coverage = EBIT ÷ interest = 45 ÷ 9 = 5, option C. Option A ratio ulta hai. Option B EBIT se pehle interest ghata deta hai ((45 − 9) ÷ 9); coverage EBIT par hi nikalta hai. Option D sirf difference (45 − 9) hai.

questions.question: Fictional 'Kanchan Pharma' (₹ crore): current assets 200 (jisme inventories 80 aur prepaid expenses 10), current liabilities 125. Quick ratio kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Quick ratio = (current assets − inventories − prepaid expenses) ÷ current liabilities = (200 − 80 − 10) ÷ 125 = 110 ÷ 125 = 0.88, option A. Option B sirf inventory hataata hai, prepaid bhool kar (120 ÷ 125). Option C current ratio hai. Option D inventory ko hi numerator bana deta hai (80 ÷ 125).

questions.question: Fictional distributor 'Amrit Agencies' ka saal ka revenue ₹540 crore, COGS ₹360 crore aur closing trade receivables ₹72 crore hain. Receivables days (DSO, 365 din) kitne hain?
questions.explanation: DSO = receivables ÷ revenue × 365 = 72 ÷ 540 × 365 ≈ 48.7 din, option A. Option B receivables turnover hai (540 ÷ 72), din nahi. Option C 365 se multiply karna bhool jaata hai. Option D revenue ki jagah COGS le leta hai (72 ÷ 360 × 365); receivables sale price par bante hain, isliye revenue se compare hote hain.

questions.question: Fictional retailer 'Sarita Mart' ka revenue ₹600 crore, net profit margin 6%, average total assets ₹400 crore aur average equity ₹200 crore hai. ROA aur ROE kitne hain?
questions.explanation: PAT = 600 × 6% = ₹36 crore. ROA = net margin × asset turnover = 6% × (600 ÷ 400) = 9% (ya 36 ÷ 400). ROE = 36 ÷ 200 = 18%; assets ka aadha hi equity hai, baaki debt se, isliye ROE ROA ka doguna hai. Option D. Option A net margin ko hi ROA maan leta hai. Option B ROA ko 2 se multiply karne ki jagah divide karta hai. Option C ROE ko net margin samajh leta hai.

questions.question: Fictional listed company 'Tulsi Agro Ltd' ka PAT ₹30 crore hai, jisme se ₹2 crore preference dividend dena hai. Company ke 4 crore equity shares hain aur share price ₹105 hai. EPS aur P/E ratio kya hain?
questions.explanation: EPS = (PAT − preference dividend) ÷ equity shares = (30 − 2) ÷ 4 = ₹7. P/E = 105 ÷ 7 = 15, option B. Option A preference dividend ghataana bhool jaata hai (30 ÷ 4 = 7.5, 105 ÷ 7.5 = 14). Option C ratio ulta (EPS ÷ price) leta hai. Option D preference dividend ko jod deta hai (32 ÷ 4).

questions.question: Fictional 'Navya Fashions' ke Q1 (3 mahine) ka revenue ₹90 crore hai aur Q1 end par trade receivables ₹60 crore hain. Analyst annual definition (revenue ko annualise karke, 365 din) se DSO nikaalna chahta hai. DSO kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Quarterly flow ko annualise karo: ₹90 crore × 4 = ₹360 crore. DSO = 60 ÷ 360 × 365 ≈ 60.8 din, option C. Option A quarterly revenue ko seedha annual ki tarah use karta hai (60 ÷ 90 × 365), jisse DSO chaar guna ho jaata hai. Option B sirf 2 se annualise karta hai, aur option D 12 se (jaise revenue monthly ho).

questions.question: Do fictional companies ka EBIT ₹20 crore hai aur tax 25%. 'Ojas Ltd' ke paas koi debt nahi, equity ₹100 crore. 'Prana Ltd' ke paas ₹50 crore debt 10% interest par aur equity ₹50 crore. Dono ka ROE (PAT ÷ equity) kitna hai?

Option B Prana ka interest bhool jaata hai (15 ÷ 50). Option C tax bhool jaata hai (pre-tax numbers).

weeks.title: Case Study: Reading One Company's Statements End to End
weeks.summary: Is week aap ek fictional company ke do saal ke statements par poora analysis karoge: growth, margins, working capital days, coverage, cash conversion aur free cash flow, aur seekhoge ki numbers se 'kahani' aur red flags kaise nikaalte hain.
concepts: **Analysis ka order**: (1) business samjho (kya bechti hai, kisko, cash kab aata hai), (2) income statement: growth aur margins, (3) balance sheet: working capital aur leverage, (4) cash flow: profit cash mein badla ya nahi, (5) sab jod kar kahani aur sawaal. Ratios ka dher lagaane se pehle har step par ek sawaal likho jiska jawab chahiye.

**Growth aur common-size**: har line ka year-on-year growth nikaalo aur income statement ko revenue ke % mein (common-size) likho. Agar receivables ya inventory revenue se kaafi tez badh rahe hain, to growth ka quality sawaal mein hai: kya credit dhila karke ya stock bhar kar sales badhaayi gayi?

**Margin bridge**: gross margin → EBITDA margin → EBIT margin → PAT margin. Har level par dekho ki kaunsa cost revenue se tez badha. Gross margin girna aksar pricing pressure ya input cost ka sign hai; operating margin girna overheads ka.

**Working capital days**: DSO = receivables ÷ revenue × 365, DIO = inventory ÷ COGS × 365, DPO = payables ÷ COGS × 365; cash conversion cycle = DSO + DIO − DPO. Days badhne ka matlab har rupaye ki sale ke liye zyada paisa business mein phansa hai.

**Cash conversion**: CFO ÷ PAT lagbhag 1 ya usse upar hona healthy maana jaata hai (depreciation wapas judta hai). Lagataar 1 se kaafi neeche hona red flag hai: profit kaagaz par hai, cash receivables ya inventory mein. **Free cash flow** = CFO − capex; negative FCF ko debt ya equity se fund karna padta hai.
**Leverage aur coverage trend**: debt-equity aur interest coverage (EBIT ÷ interest) ko saal-dar-saal dekho. Growth debt se fund ho aur coverage gir raha ho, to agle downturn mein risk zyada hai.

**Write-up**: analysis ka output ek chhota memo hai: 3-4 key findings numbers ke saath, unke possible reasons, aur management se poochhne wale sawaal (receivables ageing, customer concentration, capex ka purpose). 'Ratio X achha hai' nahi, 'ratio X kyun badla aur iska business matlab kya hai' likho.

example.problem: Fictional 'Shakti Home Appliances Ltd' ke do saal (₹ crore, code dekho). Tax 25%. Simplification: CFO = PAT + depreciation − working capital ka badlaav (interest operating mein). FY26 ka end-to-end analysis karo.
steps: Income statement: FY26 gross profit = 480 − 322 = 158 (32.9%, FY25 mein 35.0%); EBIT = 158 − 86 − 14 = 58; PBT = 46; PAT = 34.5. FY25: EBIT 48, PBT 40, PAT 30.
Growth: revenue +20%, PAT +15%, par receivables +50% (60 → 90) aur inventory +21.4% (70 → 85).
Working capital days: DSO 54.75 se 68.4 din; DIO (inventory ÷ COGS × 365) 98.3 se 96.4 din, lagbhag stable. Problem receivables mein hai.
Working capital ka badlaav = +30 (receivables) + 15 (inventory) − 5 (payables) = 40. CFO = 34.5 + 14 − 40 = 8.5; CFO ÷ PAT ≈ 0.25.
FCF = 8.5 − capex 67 = −58.5. Funding: borrowings +50, cash 30 se 12 (−18), aur upar se dividend 9.5 bhi diya. Check: 30 + 8.5 − 67 + 50 − 9.5 = 12.
Leverage: D/E 80 ÷ 220 = 0.36 se 130 ÷ 245 = 0.53; interest coverage 48 ÷ 8 = 6.0 se 58 ÷ 12 = 4.83.

Answer (memo): **growth 20% hai par dhile credit aur debt se fund hua: margins gire, DSO ~14 din badha, CFO PAT ka sirf ~25%, FCF −58.5 crore**. Sawaal: receivables ageing, naye bade customers ke credit terms, aur ₹67 crore capex ka return.

Do saalon ke ratios alag definitions se nikaalna (ek saal average, doosre saal closing). Trend tabhi meaningful hai jab definition same ho.
Red flag ko conclusion bana dena. Badhte receivables naye bade customer ki wajah se bhi ho sakte hain; memo mein use sawaal ki tarah likho aur data (ageing) maango.
revision: Order: business → P&L → balance sheet → cash flow → memo.
Receivables/inventory ka growth revenue se compare karo.
CCC = DSO + DIO − DPO.
CFO ÷ PAT ≪ 1 lagataar = earnings quality red flag.
FCF = CFO − capex; negative ho to funding source dekho.

weeks.title: Management Accounting: Cost Behaviour, Contribution and Break-even
weeks.summary: Is week aap costs ko fixed/variable aur direct/indirect mein classify karna, high-low method se mixed cost todna, contribution margin, break-even, margin of safety, target profit, operating leverage aur multi-product break-even nikaalna seekhoge.
concepts: **Management vs financial accounting**: financial accounting bahar ke users (investors, lenders, tax) ke liye rules (Ind AS) ke hisaab se past report karta hai. Management accounting andar ke decisions ke liye hai: pricing, product mix, budget, make-or-buy. Yahan koi fixed format nahi; jo decision ke liye relevant ho wahi numbers. Analyst ka zyada kaam isi side hota hai.

**Cost behaviour**: **variable cost** volume ke saath badhta hai (raw material, packaging, sales commission); **fixed cost** ek relevant range mein volume se nahi badalta (rent, salaried staff, software licence); **mixed (semi-variable)** dono ka mix (electricity: fixed connection charge + per-unit usage). Per unit dekho to ulta: variable cost per unit constant, fixed cost per unit volume badhne par girta hai.

**Direct vs indirect**: direct cost kisi cost object (product, customer, branch) se seedha trace hota hai (us product ka material); indirect (overhead) kai objects mein share hota hai aur allocate karna padta hai (factory manager ki salary). Direct/indirect aur fixed/variable alag sawaal hain: product line ke supervisor ki salary direct bhi hai aur fixed bhi.

**High-low method**: mixed cost ko todne ka simple tareeka: variable rate = (highest activity par cost − lowest activity par cost) ÷ (activity ka farak); fixed part = total cost − variable rate × activity. Analyst sab data points par linear regression se bhi yahi karta hai (slope = variable rate, intercept = fixed), jo outliers se kam prabhavit hota hai.

**Contribution margin (CM)**: CM per unit = price − variable cost per unit; CM ratio = CM ÷ price. Har bechi gayi unit pehle fixed costs cover karti hai, phir profit deti hai. Profit = units × CM − fixed costs.

**Break-even aur target profit**: break-even units = fixed costs ÷ CM per unit; break-even revenue = fixed costs ÷ CM ratio. Target profit ke liye units = (fixed costs + target profit) ÷ CM. **Margin of safety** = (actual sales − break-even sales) ÷ actual sales: sales kitne % gir sakte hain loss se pehle.

**Operating leverage**: DOL = total contribution ÷ operating profit (EBIT). Sales x% badhe to EBIT lagbhag DOL × x% badhta hai (CM ratio aur fixed cost same rahein to exactly). High fixed cost business (software, airlines) ka DOL zyada: upside mein profit tezi se badhta hai, downside mein tezi se girta hai. DOL = 1 ÷ margin of safety.

**Multi-product break-even**: sales mix ko ek 'bundle' maano (jaise 3 A + 2 B), bundle ka CM nikaalo, fixed costs ÷ bundle CM = bundles, phir mix se units. Mix badla to break-even bhi badlega; products ka simple average CM lena galat hai jab mix barabar na ho.

example.problem: Fictional 'Dhaara Water Purifiers' ek purifier ₹12,000 mein bechti hai; variable cost ₹7,200 per unit; monthly fixed costs ₹48 lakh. Is mahine 1,250 units bikne ka forecast hai. CM, break-even, profit, margin of safety aur DOL nikaalo.
steps: Break-even units = 48,00,000 ÷ 4,800 = 1,000 units; break-even revenue = 48,00,000 ÷ 0.40 = ₹1.2 crore.
1,250 units par total contribution = 1,250 × 4,800 = ₹60 lakh; profit = 60 − 48 = ₹12 lakh.
Matlab: sales 10% badhe to profit lagbhag 50% badhega; sales 20% gire to break-even.
Answer: **CM ₹4,800 (40%), BEP 1,000 units, profit ₹12 lakh, MoS 20%, DOL 5**.

mistakes: Fixed cost per unit ko variable cost maan kar decisions lena. 1,000 units par ₹4,800 per unit fixed lag raha hai, par 1,250 par sirf ₹3,840; per-unit fixed number volume badalne par badalta hai.
Break-even ke liye fixed cost ko price se divide karna. Har unit sirf apna contribution (price − variable cost) fixed cost ki taraf deti hai.
Multi-product mein products ke CM ka simple average lena jab sales mix barabar na ho. Mix ke weights se bundle CM nikaalo.
revision: CM = price − VC; CM ratio = CM ÷ price.
BEP units = FC ÷ CM; BEP revenue = FC ÷ CM ratio.
Target units = (FC + target profit) ÷ CM.
High-low: VC rate = Δcost ÷ Δactivity; FC = cost − rate × activity.
DOL = contribution ÷ EBIT = 1 ÷ MoS.
Multi-product: bundle CM se break-even, phir mix se units.
